subject: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up for ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up for ACME

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery:

- Goal: ship an LLM-enhanced help center that can safely summarize customer tickets and surface recommended KB articles with <200ms response target for common queries.
- Key constraints: PII redaction required (names, emails, account IDs), occasional long transcripts (up to ~6k chars), and budget sensitivity on high-throughput paths.
- Recommended model candidates (initial): Redwood-2.1 (balanced accuracy/latency), OpenModelX-13B-8q (cost-optimized), and a distilled 3B for high-volume low-cost fallbacks. We’ll run a short eval on your prompt set to validate quality/regressions.

Action items for ACME: please send us a representative prompt set (10–20 examples is fine to start) that includes:
  1) Typical user queries you expect (short & conversational)
  2) One or two long-ticket transcripts for summarization
  3) Edge cases where the model should not return PII or should redacted content
  4) Any hard rejection triggers (examples of hallucination-sensitive outcomes)

Optional but helpful: a few examples of expected output (gold labels) and any existing redaction rules you use today. We can provide a CSV template if that helps.

We’ll prioritize running the model-fit eval once we have the prompts and will share a short dashboard with per-prompt regression flags and recommended config (quantization, batching) within 48 hours.

Attachment: prompt_set_template.csv (simple CSV with columns: id, input_text, expected_output, redaction_flag)

Thanks — looping in Vivek and Rishi to support the prompt collection and redaction guidance.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0132
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up for ACME

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — appreciate the clear checklist. I attached an initial prompt set (ACME_prompt_set_v1.csv) and a short doc describing our current redaction rules (redaction_examples.txt). A couple of notes:

- We included 15 prompts: 8 short user queries, 4 ticket transcripts (one long ~5k chars), and 3 flagged edge cases.
- Our redaction rules: we remove account numbers (ACC-XXXXX), SSNs, and emails before storage. However, some fields are retained in the ticket text for context (e.g., masked account id ACC-123**).
- Concern: we’ve seen models incorrectly reveal masked PII if prompts are phrased like "what was the customer’s email?" — we’d prefer model-level redaction or a strict classifier that rejects PII-extraction requests.

We’re happy to add gold answers where helpful. Do you need any additional metadata columns in the CSV?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Support Automation
ACME Corp
samantha.lee@acme.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up for ACME

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the files. Quick guidance on redaction and edge cases:

- Recommended approach: do a two-step pipeline for sensitive outputs: (1) model generation constrained to the task (summarization/retrieval) + (2) a lightweight PII classifier/post-processing filter that blocks or redacts any detected PII. We can provide an open-source regex/classifier bundle that runs sub-10ms per response for common PII types.
- For masked tokens (ACC-123**), please include a "mask_mode" column in your CSV indicating whether the masked token should be treated as sensitive context-only or can be surfaced. That helps the eval to flag regressions.
- Edge-case examples: please include prompts that intentionally try to elicit PII (e.g., "what is the customer email associated with ticket #12345?") so we can validate the model rejects or redacts.
- Regarding models: Redwood-2.1 tends to be better at following instruction-style constraints; OpenModelX-13B-8q is cost-efficient but sometimes needs stricter system prompts + filtering. We’ll report per-model precision/recall on redaction and hallucination risk.

I’ll upload a short redaction filter we use internally and a sample CSV header in the next email.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up for ACME

Samantha —

This is great, thank you for sending the prompt set and redaction doc. Quick checklist before we run the eval:

- Please confirm the three flagged prompts are intentional tests (yes/no).
- If possible, add a "mask_mode" column as Vivek suggested (sensitive_context | reveal_allowed). If you can’t, we’ll assume masked tokens are sensitive_context.
- If you have any gold outputs for the 4 summarization examples, please attach them — they speed up regression detection.

Next steps from our side:
- Vivek will run the redaction classifier + run model-fit eval across the three candidate profiles (Redwood-2.1, OpenModelX-13B-8q, Distil-3B fallback). We’ll prioritize the long-transcript summarization and the PII-extraction edge cases.
- Expected deliverable: a short deck and an eval dashboard link showing: per-prompt pass/fail for redaction, quality scores, latency estimates, and recommended config (quantization level, batch size, caching hints) within 48 hours of final CSV.

Related links: Eval dashboard (we’ll send once ready) — I also created a HubSpot note: https://hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345

Thanks again — looking forward to the prompt revisions.

Best,
Marissa
